newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia's Nujoma urges better life for his people.
newsitem.headline: Namibia's Nujoma urges better life for his people.

text.p: Namibia's President Sam Nujoma urged his 72-member parliament on Tuesday to improve the lives of ordinary Namibians after seven years of black majority rule.

"Political stability and parliamentary procedures will be meaningless unless they are backed by real changes in the lives of the majority of our people. We must work hard to improve their standard of living which is less than satisfactory," Nujoma told the opening of parliament.
He said hard work, self-reliance and accountable government were needed to achieving this goal.

Referring to Namibia's peaceful transition from white South African administration to independence in March 1990, he said the country had succeeded in establishing a stable democratic system but much needed to be done to improve people's lives.

Formerly known as South West Africa, Namibia was ruled by South Africa for 75 years. It became independent under a U.N.-sponsored peace plan linked to the withdrawal of Cuban troops from neighbouring Angola. Nujoma's South West African People's Organisation won elections in November 1989.

Although Nujoma has produced one of the most democratic administrations in Africa, he has been criticised by opposition politicans for failing to improve the lives of Namibians, which could cost him elections scheduled for 1998.

Nujoma said development of Namibia could only be achieved through good governance: "It can only take place if the leadership of this country provides the necessary guidance and commits itself to the principles of responsibility, transparency, honesty and accountability."
The president said rising crime, a high number of teenage pregancies, lack of employment opportunities and continued discrimination against women were worrying.

But Nujoma said funds for drought relief could be channelled to other projects after good rains this year. He said Namibia's development plan aimed at alleviating poverty and private sector job creation was well underway.
